definitions.explanation: Leaves growing on or fallen from a tree. Often evokes a literary or seasonal image.

examples.japanese: {木|こ}の{葉|は}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{散|ち}った→散る：02075_chiru⟧。

examples.english: When autumn comes, the leaves turn red.

examples.japanese: ⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{吹|ふ}かれて→吹く：02445_fuku⟧{木|こ}の{葉|は}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦くるくる→くるくる：05352_kurukuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{舞|ま}い{落|お}ちた→舞い落ちる：18207_maiochiru⟧。
examples.english: Blown by the wind, the leaves spiraled down.

notes:
{木|こ}の{葉|は} specifically refers to leaves of a tree, often with a literary or poetic nuance. Commonly evokes autumn imagery.

PRONUNCIATION:
The standard reading is ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧. The kanji {木|こ}の{葉|は} uses the kun'yomi of both characters. An alternative reading きの⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ also exists but is less common.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧: leaf (general, neutral)
- ⟦{葉|は}っぱ→葉っぱ：05388_happa⟧: leaf (casual, slightly childlike)
- {木|こ}の{葉|は}: tree leaves (literary, evocative)
{木|こ}の{葉|は} tends to appear in descriptions of nature, poetry, and seasonal imagery, while ⟦{葉|は}っぱ→葉っぱ：05388_happa⟧ is the everyday word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {木|こ}の{葉|は}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{散|ち}る→散る：02075_chiru⟧: leaves fall/scatter
- {木|こ}の{葉|は}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{揺|ゆ}れる→揺れる：01161_yureru⟧: leaves sway
- {木|こ}の{葉|は}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{舞|ま}う→舞う：04573_mau⟧: leaves dance (in the wind)
- ⟦{枯|か}れ{葉|は}→枯れ葉：20386_kareha⟧: dead/withered leaves
